title: Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 (No. 38, 2026), as made, C2026A00038
used_for: Definitions (s 761GB digital token, s 86 possession, s 761GC DAP, s 761GD TCP, s 9E PDTI, s 9F custodial staking, s 765E wrapped tokens); DAPs/TCPs as financial products (s 764A(1)(la)-(lb)); constitutionally-covered corporation rule (s 766M, s 9); new dealing (s 766C(1)(ca)); exemptions (s 911A(2)(ja)-(jb), s 911A(4B), s 766A(3)(b)); operator duties (ss 912BB-912BI, 1020AN-1020AR); fundraising (ss 741A-741B); commencement (s 2) and transition (ss 1730-1735); second reading speech dates (endnote).

title: ASIC's roadmap for digital assets law reform implementation
used_for: Passage on 1 April 2026; 18-month implementation timeline; original statement of 9 April 2027 commencement; duty to comply with existing licensing during implementation; indicative content of asset-holding and transactional and settlement standards (Table 1); 'Month 18 onwards' full implementation.

title: 26-245MR ASIC consults on implementation of new digital asset laws
used_for: Laws commence 8 April 2027; 'same activity, same risk, same regulatory outcome' and Commissioner Kirkland quote; what firms will need to do; consultation closes 5pm AEDT 27 November 2026; no-action period October 2025 to 30 September 2026; over 140 applications; Project Acacia (2025-26); Government regulatory design in parallel.

title: CP 392 Digital asset law reform implementation: Proposed standards and guidance (landing page and downloads)
used_for: Contents of the consultation package: draft regulatory guide, draft asset-holding standards, draft transactional and settlement standards, draft financial requirements.

title: Consultation Paper 392 (CP 392), Digital asset law reform implementation: Proposed standards and guidance (PDF)
used_for: Timeline (p 5: stages 1-6, incl. 8 April 2027 and 7 October 2027); purpose of the Act (paras 2-5); payments reforms (paras 6-7); international context (paras 8-9); risk warning (para 14); transparency (para 22); exemptions list (para 38); authorisation needed from 8 October 2027 (para 39); apply by 7 October 2027 (para 45); proposal A4 (list of applicants); platform vs asset protections (para 53); proposal B5 (wallet and address reporting); Section D (three NTA options); Table 9 (proposed INFO 225 guidance on PDTI).

title: Attachment 1 to CP 392: Draft Regulatory Guide 000 Digital asset platforms and tokenised custody platforms (draft RG 000)
used_for: RG 000.7-000.8 (regime overview, operators need an AFS licence); RG 000.20 (platform is a separate financial product); RG 000.22 note (INFO 225 update before finalisation in early 2027); Figure 1 (seven questions); RG 000.35 and note (what is not a TCP; native tokenised fund generally a managed investment scheme); RG 000.36-000.42 (DAP definition and what is not a DAP, incl. MPC technology providers); RG 000.43 (agents); RG 000.46-000.48 (tokens that are financial products); RG 000.60-000.62 (markets and CS facilities); RG 000.67, Table 2, RG 000.80 (financial services around platforms); Table 3 (exemptions, incl. anticipated regulations and inflation indexing); RG 000.76; RG 000.78; RG 000.82-000.84 (no corporate authorised representative issue; authorised intermediary exemption); Table 4 (issue authorisations by business model).

title: User guide for CP 392: Digital asset law reform implementation, consultation package reader guide (PDF)
used_for: Plain descriptions of DAPs and TCPs (TCP example: assets held in custody such as gold); new ASIC standards commencing 8 April 2027.

title: ASIC extends no-action position for digital asset businesses to 30 September 2026
used_for: Extension of the INFO 225 sector-wide no-action position from 30 June 2026 to 30 September 2026; expanded scope (authorised representative and intermediary arrangements).

title: 25-250MR Updated ASIC guidance supports digital asset innovation and boosts investor protection
used_for: Updated INFO 225; tokenised securities among products ASIC considers financial products; sector-wide no-action position initially to 30 June 2026.

title: Deadline looms for digital asset businesses to apply for a licence
used_for: Earlier ASIC statement that the Act 'will commence on 9 April 2027' (used only to explain the date difference).

title: Tokeniser homepage, including FAQ ('Is Tokeniser regulated?', 'What about compliance?')
used_for: Tokeniser operates on Redbelly Network; 'Products issued through Tokeniser operate under an Asset Issuer's existing licensing'; eligibility programmed into every asset; Tokeniser is a Redbelly Network project.

title: Tokeniser: Our Technology
used_for: Tokeniser's statements that Redbelly is designed to meet the three statutory tests for public digital token infrastructure, and that settlement, secondary liquidity and collateral mobility sit in an 'exempt protocol layer'.

title: Tokeniser: Protocol Finance
used_for: Use of ERC-3643 and ERC-7575 structures; Tokeniser's own 'Guardrails' (offer still regulated; regulations can move the line; critical participant test; rights attached to tokens).

title: Tokeniser: Automated compliance
used_for: Pre-trade eligibility checks, logging of every check; 'Engineered to align with Australia's Digital Assets Framework, operating under your existing licence'.

title: Tokeniser Knowledge Hub: How does Tokeniser handle investor compliance?
used_for: KYC/AML and investor classification before wallet activation; rules encoded into the token and checked at every transfer; on-chain compliance records.

title: Tokeniser Knowledge Hub: What is self-custodial asset administration?
used_for: Investors hold tokens in their own wallets; Tokeniser designed for professional fund administration, not retail self-custody; provides key management and recovery mechanisms.

title: Redbelly Network: Asset Tokenisation
used_for: Redbelly describes itself as public digital token infrastructure; verifiable credentials and eligibility at point of trade; AML/CTF/Travel Rule applied 'as needed ... without restricting access at the network level'.

title: Redbelly Network Technical Documentation (Receptor; Onboarding and Eligibility Kit)
used_for: Redbelly is a layer 1 blockchain built for real-world asset tokenisation; Receptor and the Eligibility SDK.

title: Redbelly docs: IndividualOnboardingSDK overview
used_for: Onboarding includes wallet authentication, KYC verification and Redbelly on-chain permission setup.

title: Redbelly Developer Portal (Vine): Eligibility on Redbelly
used_for: Programmable eligibility criteria via Receptor; Proof by Query (zero-knowledge, on chain) and Selective Disclosure (off chain); developers decide which issuers they trust; accredited issuers for network access credentials.

title: Redbelly Developer Portal (Vine): Verifiable credentials
used_for: Receptor is built on the W3C verifiable credential model (issuer, holder, verifier).

title: Redbelly Developer Portal (Vine): Accessing Redbelly Network
used_for: Users must claim an access credential from a network accredited issuer (passport with biometric checks) before enabling write access.

title: Redbelly Developer Portal (Vine): Accredited issuers
used_for: 'On Redbelly, all network participants must prove they are who they say they are in order to get network access.'

title: Redbelly Developer Portal (Vine): Become an operator
used_for: Node operators need network access for two accounts, must stake 100,000 RBNT, apply and are selected on experience, location and commitment; submissions currently closed.

title: Redbelly Developer Portal (Vine): DBFT and super block (Consensus)
used_for: Leaderless DBFT consensus; deterministic (quasi-instant) finality; Redbelly states the chain cannot fork.

title: ERC-3643: T-REX - Token for Regulated EXchanges
used_for: Standard requires an on-chain identity system, a recovery system, the ability to freeze investor wallets, pause, and agent forced transfers; compliance check on each transfer.

title: Redbelly Network: Project Acacia
used_for: Redbelly's statement that it was selected for the Reserve Bank of Australia's Project Acacia pilot as part of NotCentralised's securitisation use case.
